column6: This exception occurs because the bank has recorded the ₹81,000 transaction (TXN017) twice, whereas Razorpay only processed a single valid entry. This is most likely caused by a technical processing glitch, network retry, or duplicate settlement processing on the bank's end during clearing. To resolve this, contact the partner bank to confirm the duplicate entry and request a reversal so the bank statement aligns with Razorpay's records.

This exception indicates that a payment of ₹50,000 was successfully captured in Razorpay (TXN007), but no corresponding deposit has been credited to your bank account. The most likely cause is a standard settlement processing delay due to banking cut-off times, weekend delays, or standard gateway payout timelines (e.g., T+1/T+2 days). To resolve this, check the Razorpay dashboard to verify the transaction's settlement status and UTR number, and escalate to Razorpay support if the payout exceeds the agreed settlement SLA.

This exception indicates that transaction TXN050 for 630 was processed successfully in Razorpay but is not yet reflected on your bank statement, which is most likely caused by standard settlement processing delays or bank cut-off timing. To resolve this, check the settlement batch status in the Razorpay dashboard to confirm if the funds are queued for payout, or wait for the next business day's bank statement to confirm receipt.

This exception means a credit of 9,900 was recorded in your bank account without any corresponding transaction record in Razorpay. This is most likely caused by a customer making a direct bank transfer (such as via NEFT or IMPS) that bypassed the payment gateway, or an uncaptured payment due to a webhook failure. To resolve this, review the bank statement's remitter details and UTR number to identify the payer, then manually map or log the transaction in your system.
